key: And he stood between the dead and the living; and the plague was stayed.
s: After the people blame Moses and Aaron for Korah’s dead, a plague begins and Aaron runs in with incense; Rashi, on Numbers 17:13, reads the incense as God’s answer to those who called it deadly poison: it stays plague, and sin is what kills.

evidence.words: דָּ"אַ, לָמָּה בַקְּטֹרֶת? לְפִי שֶׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מְלִיזִים וּמְרַנְּנִים אַחַר הַקְּטֹרֶת לוֹמַר סַם הַמָּוֶת הוּא — עַל יָדוֹ מֵתוּ נָדָב וַאֲבִיהוּא, עַל יָדוֹ נִשְׂרְפוּ חֲמִשִּׁים וּמָאתַיִם אִישׁ — אָמַר הַקָּבָּ"ה, תִּרְאוּ שֶׁעוֹצֵר מַגֵּפָה הוּא וְהַחֵטְא הוּא הַמֵּמִית
evidence.gloss: [Rashi on 17:13, second explanation:] Another explanation: why with the incense? Because Israel were disparaging and murmuring against the incense, saying it is a deadly poison: through it Nadab and Abihu died, through it the two hundred and fifty men were burnt. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: you will see that it holds back plague, and it is sin that kills.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref Numbers 17:13 and at [133,13] match). Plain sense faithful to 17:6 to 12: the congregation charges Moses and Aaron with killing the people, the plague begins, Aaron runs into the assembly with incense; no four-word run from the key verse. Rashi on 17:13, in his second explanation (davar acher, citing the Mekhilta), says Israel murmured that the incense was a deadly poison (Nadab and Abihu, the 250 men) and God said they would see it holds back plague and sin is what kills: the sentence carries exactly this. His first explanation (Aaron holding back the angel) is a different reading, not contradicted. Rashbam and Sforno on the verse do not touch the incense. entry-check ok.
